source.title: Studying inductive biases in image classification task

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is supplied.
record.tranche_reason: Ablates local connectivity and spatial invariance in ResNet50-based ImageNet classifiers, measuring validation accuracy. This bears conceptually on the architecture comparison, though the study does not compare fully connected networks.
record.gate_note: Reports validation-accuracy outcomes for architecture and inductive-bias ablations. It does not measure training error, test error, or the training–test gap; it does not test random-label memorization.
record.test_reason: The study measures ImageNet validation accuracy for convolution, locally connected depthwise filters, and local attention variants. It does not compare convolutional with fully connected networks or isolate local connectivity against full connectivity, as V3 requires. Its spatial-sharing and context-awareness ablations address related architectural questions. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors conclude that context awareness matters, small local contexts suffice to construct filters, and relaxing spatial invariance improves accuracy while eliminating it makes training harder. Relative position encoding remains helpful. They also conclude that strong locality is more important for downsampling filters than spatial filters, and relaxed spatial invariance can mitigate that downsampling constraint.
record.recipe_differences: ImageNet ResNet50-D ablations of depthwise convolution and context-aware decomposed attention; reports validation accuracy, not train/test error or generalization gap. Uses synchronous SGD, 256 minibatch, 120 epochs, and basic augmentation for the main ablations.
record.method_sensitivity: Accuracy changes with spatial invariance, number of base kernels, context awareness, CA-kernel and aggregation-kernel size, number of heads, downsampling-filter design, BN/ReLU, and training scheme. Several plots report trends without exact values.

fits_no_version.finding: A locally connected depthwise network reaches 76.68% Top-1 accuracy versus 78.40% for spatially shared depthwise convolution.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spatial weight sharing improves ImageNet accuracy in the tested locally connected depthwise architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Relaxing spatial invariance through additional context-aware base kernels improves accuracy overall, with an irregular trend for the stage-doubling schedule.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Partial relaxation of spatial weight sharing can improve local attention network accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Omitting BN/ReLU improves the two tested CADA configurations from 77.89% to 78.64% and from 77.85% to 78.99%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The placement of normalization and activation affects accuracy in these CADA architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: CADA network A reaches 78.64%, compared with 78.05% for multihead depthwise convolution and 78.13% for non-context-aware DA network D.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Context-aware filter construction improves accuracy in the tested local filtering architectures.

record.code_released: https://github.com/hszhao/SAN (implementation followed; no study-specific code release stated)
record.problems: The study reports maximum Top-1 validation accuracy and does not report training error or a train–test gap. It does not compare fully connected networks. Several findings are shown only in figures; no uncertainty estimates are stated. The authors say they did not conduct an extensive hyper-parameter search.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible numeric results were left out. Some plotted ablations of head size, kernel sizes, and downsampling filters are not included because they are architecture-accuracy measurements that do not directly test the version's convolution-versus-fully-connected comparison; plotted values are figure-only.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe; chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error, with networks trained to convergence.

Convolutional versus fully connected performance; the contribution of local connectivity to that difference; learning sparse local connections in fully connected networks; initialization from trained convolutional networks.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover large-batch performance.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps or ranking relative to other measures.
Removing examples selected by label-memorization influence versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Held-out validation accuracy is a suitable generalization-performance measure for V3; absence of a training–test gap is not the reason for exclusion. The missing comparison is convolutional versus fully connected networks, or an experiment isolating the local-connectivity contribution named in V3. The paper cites original V3 sources, but its own results address different architectural properties.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization, natural-label generalization relative to chance, and training–test error.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold and test error.

Fully connected networks, the cited LeCun and d’Ascoli comparisons, and initializing a fully connected network from trained convolutional weights. The study uses ImageNet ResNet50 variants and validation accuracy, not a training–test generalization gap.

rows.subject: 7 × 7 locally-connected DW network
rows.stage_stated: trained; training details not stated for this comparison
rows.operation_detail: Compared locally-connected depthwise network with 7 × 7 DW convolution on ImageNet classification.
rows.note: The paper describes the locally-connected result as significantly worse. This comparison relaxes spatial invariance while retaining local depthwise connectivity.
rows.check: The numbers are correct, but both networks retain local connectivity. The comparison tests spatial weight sharing, not V3's convolution-versus-fully-connected advantage. Lower accuracy without sharing is not a reversal of V3.

rows.subject: CADA, b = (i, i, i, i)
rows.size_stated: Network size varied; b denotes number of base kernels
rows.operation_detail: Varied the same number of base kernels in each layer to relax spatial invariance.
rows.baseline: DW convolution reference shown in Fig. 8
rows.note: The text states that this setting showed steady accuracy improvement as network size increased; exact values are only plotted.
rows.check: Increasing base-kernel counts changes capacity and spatial invariance within local attention networks. It does not test V3 or V2's widening beyond zero training error. Exact plotted values are not recorded.

rows.subject: CADA, b = (j, 2j, 4j, 8j)
rows.size_stated: Network size varied; b denotes number of base kernels
rows.operation_detail: Varied base kernels by doubling the count at each stage to relax spatial invariance.
rows.baseline: DW convolution reference shown in Fig. 8
rows.note: The text calls this schedule unstable, but says it still gave better accuracy than DW convolution.
rows.check: The stage-dependent base-kernel sweep measures local attention architecture performance, without a fully connected comparator or interpolation-threshold measurement. Its irregular accuracy trend does not establish a partial V3 effect.

rows.subject: CADAsp, b = (4, 4, 4, 4)
rows.operation_detail: Compared CADAsp with and without BN and ReLU in the ImageNet classification task.
rows.note: This is an architecture-component ablation; it reports validation accuracy, not generalization gap.
rows.check: Table 4 and its accompanying text identify the tested architecture as CADA, not CADAsp. The reported 77.89% versus 78.64% is a BN/ReLU ablation, unrelated to the versions.

rows.subject: CADAsp, b = (8, 16, 32, 64)
rows.operation_detail: Compared CADAsp with and without BN and ReLU in the ImageNet classification task.
rows.note: This is an architecture-component ablation; it reports validation accuracy, not generalization gap.
rows.check: Table 4 and its accompanying text identify the tested architecture as CADA, not CADAsp. The reported 77.85% versus 78.99% is a BN/ReLU ablation, unrelated to the versions.

rows.subject: 7 × 7 DW convolution
rows.operation_detail: Compared with CADA and CADAsp variants that add context awareness and base kernels.
rows.note: Baseline accuracy reported for comparison; the table does not state a no-intervention training–test gap.
rows.check: The 78.05% value is a valid depthwise-convolution comparator for the paper's architecture experiments, but alone provides no comparison required by any version.

rows.subject: CADA, network A, b = (4, 4, 4, 4)
rows.operation_detail: Added context-aware filter construction relative to the DW convolution comparator.
rows.note: Architecture comparison; accuracy is slightly higher than the listed DW convolution comparator.
rows.check: The 78.64% versus 78.05% comparison adds context-aware filter construction and relaxes spatial invariance. Both architectures retain local connectivity; neither is the fully connected comparator named in V3.

rows.subject: DA, network D
rows.operation_detail: Removed context awareness from decomposed attention.
rows.note: A non-CA decomposed-attention architecture comparison; the authors say DAsp gave similar results to DA and no significant difference from DW convolution in tested comparisons.
rows.check: The reported values compare context-aware and non-context-aware decomposed attention. This does not measure V3's convolution-versus-fully-connected advantage.

rows.subject: 7 × 7 locally-connected DW network
rows.stage_stated: trained; details not stated for this comparison
rows.operation_detail: Compared locally-connected filters with spatially shared convolution on ImageNet.
rows.note: Duplicate-free row coverage would omit this repeated textual comparison; retained here because the study explicitly uses it to argue for spatial invariance.
rows.check: Duplicates R1 and should be removed. The spatial-weight-sharing comparison does not test V3.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ImageNet ResNet50 comparison of locally-connected DW filters and spatially shared DW convolution
reader_labels.reason: The locally-connected variant has lower reported Top-1 accuracy than shared DW convolution (R1). This supports the local spatial-sharing advantage in this setting, but does not establish a fully connected comparison.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ImageNet ResNet50 variants relaxing spatial invariance with CADA base kernels
reader_labels.reason: Relaxed spatial invariance improves accuracy in the plotted sweeps, but the stage-doubling schedule is unstable and the paper reports only validation accuracy (R2, R3).
